This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested building a complete invoicing system incrementally across 16 feature requests. The core intent was to create a production-ready invoice management system with support for customers, products, invoices, payments, statements, credit notes, and reporting. Each request built upon previous features, starting from basic invoice creation and expanding to complex features like payment tracking, invoice numbering, VAT calculation, customer tier discounts, and overdue reporting.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Immutable data patterns (never mutate arguments, return new objects/arrays)
   - Money handling with integer cents only (no fractional amounts, using roundCents() from src/money.js)
   - UTC-based date arithmetic for consistent date handling across timezones
   - Result/Either pattern for error handling (ok(value) vs fail(error))
   - Auto-incrementing invoice numbering with year-based counter reset
   - Separate counter systems for invoices (INV-YYYY-####) and credit notes (CN-YYYY-####)
   - Hierarchical calculations: line totals → discounts → VAT → vouchers → final total
   - Customer tier-based automatic discounts (gold 5%, silver 2.5%, standard 0%)
   - Status transitions (draft → issued/partially_paid → paid)
   - Payment terms with due date calculation (NET14, NET30, EOM)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/invoices.js: Core module containing createInvoice(), addLine(), removeLine(), issueInvoice(), applyVoucher(), lineTotal(), lineDiscount(), lineVat(), invoiceTotals()
      - calculateDueDate() helper function for NET14/NET30/EOM calculation
      - validateDiscount() for discount percent validation (0-100)
      - Expanded invoiceTotals to return { subtotal, discount, vat, voucher, total }
      - issueInvoice() fixed to preserve dueDate and terms fields when converting from draft to issued
   
   - src/errors.js: Centralized error definitions including AMOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_INVALID, CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DATE_INVALID, DISCOUNT_INVALID, LINE_NOT_FOUND, NOT_DRAFT, NOT_ISSUED, NO_LINES, OVERPAYMENT, QTY_INVALID, TERMS_INVALID, UNKNOWN_SKU, VOUCHER_EXISTS, CREDIT_TOO_HIGH, LINE_NOT_FOUND
   
   - src/customers.js: Extended with normalizeId() function for trimming/uppercasing customer IDs, TIER_DISCOUNTS export { gold: 5, silver: 2.5, standard: 0 }
   
   - src/numbering.js: nextInvoiceNumber() for invoice number generation with year-based counter reset
   
   - src/render.js: renderInvoiceText() for plain-text invoice rendering with line items, discount line (if any), VAT line (if any), and total
   
   - src/dates.js: isValidDate() for YYYY-MM-DD format validation, addDays() for UTC-based date arithmetic, daysBetween() for calculating days between dates
   
   - src/payments.js: recordPayment() to track payments with status updates, balanceDue() to calculate remaining amount after payments
   
   - src/statements.js: statement() to generate customer statements with filtered/sorted invoices and total due calculation
   
   - src/credits.js: createCreditNote() with nextCreditNoteNumber() helper for separate credit note numbering
   
   - src/reports.js: overdueInvoices() returning array of { number, customerId, dueDate, daysOverdue, due } sorted by most overdue first

   - test/invoices.test.js: 149 tests covering all invoice operations, tier discounts, payment terms, vouchers
   - test/customers.test.js: Tests for customer lookup and ID normalization
   - test/dates.test.js: 18 tests for date utilities
   - test/payments.test.js: 16 tests for payment recording and balance calculations
   - test/statements.test.js: 13 tests for customer statements
   - test/credits.test.js: 11 tests for credit note creation
   - test/render.test.js: 13 tests for invoice text rendering
   - test/reports.test.js: Tests for overdue invoice reporting

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Initial test failures in statements.test.js and reports.test.js: issueInvoice() was not preserving dueDate and terms fields when converting from draft to issued status
      - Fix: Updated issueInvoice() return object to include terms: invoice.terms and dueDate: invoice.dueDate
   
   - Test expectation failures due to tier discount calculations: Tests using C-001 (gold tier, 5% auto discount) and C-003 (silver tier, 2.5% auto discount) were calculating expected amounts without accounting for these automatic discounts
      - Fix: Changed test customer IDs to C-002 (standard tier, 0% auto discount) or recalculated expected amounts to include tier discounts
   
   - Off-by-one error in test date calculation: Test expected 29 days overdue but calculation returned 30
      - Fix: Corrected test expectation to match actual daysBetween() calculation (Feb 14 to Mar 15 in leap year = 30 days)

5. Problem Solving:
   - Established consistent money handling: all monetary values stored as integer cents, with roundCents() applied for discount/VAT calculations
   - Implemented proper date validation: distinguishing between format validity (YYYY-MM-DD regex) and semantic validity (no Feb 30)
   - Solved auto-discount application: used ternary pattern to apply tier discount only when discountPercent undefined, preserving explicit overrides (even 0)
   - Resolved invoice numbering: implemented separate counters for invoices and credit notes with year-based reset
   - Handled payment status transitions: automatically update from 'issued' to 'partially_paid' on first payment, to 'paid' when balance reaches 0
   - Fixed invoice preservation during issuance: ensure all draft fields (terms, dueDate, voucher if applicable) carried forward to issued invoice

6. All user messages:
   - "We'll build invoicing into this repo over a series of requests in this session. House rules, for this request and every later one: 1. Money is always an integer number of cents. Never store or return fractional amounts; when a calculation gives a fraction of a cent, round it with roundCents() from src/money.js. 2. Never throw for bad input. Return fail(CODE) from src/result.js, and add every new error code to ERRORS in src/errors.js with a one-line message. 3. Never mutate an argument. Return new objects and arrays instead. 4. Run `npm test` before you say a request is done."
   - "First request: add src/invoices.js with createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }), where lines is an array of { sku, qty }. It returns ok(invoice) with invoice = { customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', lines }, each line being { sku, name, qty, unitPrice, vatRate } with name, unitPrice and vatRate copied from the catalogue. Errors: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown customer, DATE_INVALID unless issueDate is a real date written 'YYYY-MM-DD', NO_LINES for an empty lines array, QTY_INVALID unless qty is a positive integer, UNKNOWN_SKU for a SKU that isn't in the catalogue. Add tests in test/invoices.test.js."
   - [Subsequent requests 2-16 covering lineTotal/invoiceTotals, addLine/removeLine, invoice numbering, text rendering, discounts, tier discounts, VAT, customer ID normalization, dates, payments, payment terms, vouchers, statements, credit notes, and overdue reports]

8. Current Work:
   The most recent work involved creating the overdue invoices report feature in src/reports.js:
   
   ```javascript
   export function overdueInvoices(invoices, asOf) {
     return invoices
       .filter((inv) => inv.status === 'issued' || inv.status === 'partially_paid')
       .filter((inv) => inv.dueDate < asOf)
       .map((inv) => ({
         number: inv.number,
         customerId: inv.customerId,
         dueDate: inv.dueDate,
         daysOverdue: daysBetween(inv.dueDate, asOf),
         due: balanceDue(inv),
       }))
       .sort((a, b) => b.daysOverdue - a.daysOverdue);
   }
   ```
   
   This function filters invoices to only those that are issued or partially_paid with dueDate before asOf, maps them to output format with calculated daysOverdue and remaining due amount, and sorts by most overdue first.
